components.note: 行 (go, road) — 行 (walk, go) splits around the middle — 街 is a road; compare 往 go and 衔.
圭 (guī) — loose hint only — 街 is jiē.

example.hanzi: 周末我们去街上逛逛吧。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen qù jiē shang guàngguang ba.
example.english: Let's go stroll the streets this weekend.
example.fact: 街 is a street with shops and activity, while 路 is a road for getting somewhere, though the two overlap. 逛街 ("wander the streets") is the everyday word for going shopping or hanging out in town. 街 mostly appears in compounds such as 大街, 街上, 街道.

examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo jiē shang yǒu hěn duō shāngdiàn.
examples.english: There are many shops on this street.

examples.hanzi: 过了这条街，右边就是医院。
examples.pinyin: Guò le zhè tiáo jiē, yòubian jiù shì yīyuàn.
examples.english: After you cross this street, the hospital is on the right.

components.note: 电 (electric) — simplified from 電: 雨 rain over 申, a lightning bolt (申 originally pictured a flash).
⺼ (flesh, form of 月) — body parts: 肚 belly, 脚 foot, 脸 face, 胖 fat; 脑 is the brain.
The right half shows hair over a skull and also sounds out 恼 nǎo and 瑙 nǎo.

example.pinyin: Wǒ de diànnǎo huài le, xūyào xiū.
example.english: My computer is broken and needs to be fixed.
example.fact: 电脑, literally "electric brain" (电 "electricity" + 脑 "brain"), is Mainland China and Taiwan's everyday word for "computer" — more technical and academic writing also uses the more literal 计算机 ("calculating machine"), roughly the difference in English between casual "computer" and formal "computing machine."

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yòng diànnǎo xiě zuòyè.
examples.english: I use a computer to do my homework.

examples.pinyin: Zhè tái diànnǎo kāijī tài màn le.
examples.english: This computer is too slow to start up.

components.note: 匸 (hiding box) — traditional 區 put several 品 (goods) in a box 匸: separate compartments, hence districts; 区 is area, in 地区.

example.pinyin: Zhège qū de jiāotōng hěn fāngbiàn.
example.english: Transport in this district is very convenient.
example.fact: 区 is a district or zone, as in 朝阳区 (a Beijing district), 郊区 (suburb), 地区 (region) and 小区 (residential compound). Careful: 区别 is read qūbié, and the surname Ōu uses the same character with a different reading.

examples.hanzi: 我们学校在市中心的一个区。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xuéxiào zài shì zhōngxīn de yí gè qū.
examples.english: Our school is in a district of the city center.

examples.pinyin: Zhège zhùzháiqū hěn ānjìng.
examples.english: This residential area is very quiet.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hitting; also in 打 hit, 推 push.
童 (tóng) is only a loose sound clue for zhuàng.

example.pinyin: Wǒ de chē bèi zhuàng le.
example.english: My car got hit.
example.fact: 撞 is a more forceful hit than 碰 (to touch or bump lightly). 撞见 means to run into someone unexpectedly, often catching them doing something, and 撞车 covers both a car crash and a clash of schedules or ideas.

examples.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, bié zhuàng dào nà zhāng zhuōzi.
examples.english: Careful, don't bump into that table.

examples.pinyin: Tā kāichē zhuàng shàng le yì kē shù.
examples.english: He drove into a tree.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 借 is a deal between people, as in 借口.
昔 (xī) — near sound — 借 is jiè; 昔 also sounds out 惜 xī and 错 cuò.

example.pinyin: Wǒ kěyǐ jiè nǐ de bǐ ma?
example.english: May I borrow your pen?
example.fact: 借 means both "borrow" and "lend", a classic source of confusion. Direction is shown by context: 借我 / 向你借 means borrow, while 借给我 means lend to me. Many people add 给 or 出 to make the lending meaning clear.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiàng péngyou jiè le yì běn shū.
examples.english: I borrowed a book from a friend.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng jiè wǒ yìbǎi kuài qián ma?
examples.english: Can you lend me a hundred yuan?

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 秒 first meant a grain's fine tip; also in 种 plant, 秋 autumn.
少 (shǎo) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 妙 miào and 纱 shā.

example.pinyin: Zhège hóngdēng hái yǒu shí miǎo.
example.english: This red light has ten seconds left.
example.fact: 秒 started as a tiny grain tip, an image of something very small, which became the unit "second". In internet slang it is a prefix for instant: 秒懂 (get it instantly), 秒回 (reply right away), 秒杀 (flash sale).

examples.pinyin: Qǐng děng wǒ sānshí miǎo.
examples.english: Please wait thirty seconds for me.

examples.hanzi: 他跑一百米只用了十二秒。
examples.pinyin: Tā pǎo yì bǎi mǐ zhǐ yòng le shí'èr miǎo.
examples.english: He ran 100 metres in only twelve seconds.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 像 resemble; 似 is to look like.
以 (yǐ) is only a loose sound hint for sì.
乎 (hū) — as a sound part it gives hū to 呼 (call out, breathe out), so 呼 and 乎 sound the same.

example.hanzi: 他似乎不太满意这个结果。
example.pinyin: Tā sìhū bú tài mǎnyì zhège jiéguǒ.
example.english: He doesn't seem too satisfied with this result.
example.fact: 似乎 is a bookish, written-register hedge word; in everyday spoken Chinese, 好像 ("seems like") fills almost the same role but sounds noticeably more casual — the kind of pair where reaching for the wrong one flags a text as either overly stiff or too informal.

examples.pinyin: Tiānkōng sìhū yào xià yǔ le.
examples.english: It seems like it's going to rain.

examples.pinyin: Tā sìhū méi tīngdǒng wǒ de huà.
examples.english: He doesn't seem to have understood what I said.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 收, 改: to drive away, set free.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fàng; 方 also in 房 fáng and 访 fǎng.
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.

example.hanzi: 他终于放下了心中的怨恨。
example.pinyin: Tā zhōngyú fàngxiàle xīnzhōng de yuànhèn.
example.english: He finally let go of the resentment in his heart.
example.fact: 放下 extends its literal meaning ("put down, lay down") into an emotional metaphor for letting go — 放下心 ("set one's mind at ease") and 放下过去 ("let go of the past") both use the same physical verb to describe releasing an emotional burden, much like English "put it down" or "let it go."

examples.hanzi: 你先放下手机，好好吃饭。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiān fàngxià shǒujī, hǎohāo chīfàn.
examples.english: Put down your phone first and eat properly.

examples.pinyin: Tā fàngxià xíngli jiù chūqù le.
examples.english: He put down his luggage and went out.

components.note: 力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.
里 (village, unit) — the bottom; the dictionary takes it as the 'unit/measure' part, as in 重量 weight, 能量. 里 is also a Chinese mile.
旦 (dàn, dawn) — the top. A loose sound clue only today: liáng/liàng vs dàn. Do not rely on it.

example.pinyin: Tuánjié jiùshì lìliang.
example.english: Unity is strength.
example.fact: 力量 usually names an abstract or collective force — physical, political, or emotional strength (精神力量, "spiritual strength") — while its near-synonym 力气 stays narrowly physical, the concrete muscle-power a single body has or lacks (没有力气, "to have no energy left").

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiāngxìn ài de lìliang.
examples.english: I believe in the power of love.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge háizi lìliang hěn dà.
examples.english: This child is very strong.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: an order is spoken.
令 (lìng, order) is a close sound clue for mìng; 令 also in 领 lǐng, 冷 lěng and 零 líng.
令 (order) — a person kneeling under a command from above. Its sound spreads to 冷 lěng, 零 líng, 铃 líng, 领 lǐng and 怜 lián.

example.pinyin: Shìbīng bìxū fúcóng mìnglìng.
example.english: Soldiers must obey orders.
example.fact: 命令 reinforces two near-synonymous halves into one word, much like 喜欢 and 应该 elsewhere in this deck: 命 alone already carries the sense of a decree spoken aloud (per its 口 "mouth" component), and 令 independently pictures a person kneeling to receive an order — together doubling down on the same core image.

examples.hanzi: 老师命令我们安静下来。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī mìnglìng wǒmen ānjìng xiàlái.
examples.english: The teacher ordered us to quiet down.

examples.pinyin: Tā xiàle yí dào mìnglìng.
examples.english: He issued an order.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: voices in unison. 同 also gives sound to 铜 tóng, 桶 tǒng, 洞 dòng.
日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.pinyin: Liǎng rén tóngshí dàodá le jīchǎng.
example.english: The two of them arrived at the airport at the same time.
example.fact: 同时 doubles as both a time adverb ("at the same time," 他们同时开始) and a sentence connector meaning roughly "moreover, besides" (同时,他也很努力, "moreover, he's also hardworking") — a shift from marking simultaneity to marking additional information.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen tóngshí kāishǐ ba.
examples.english: Let's start at the same time.

examples.hanzi: 她一边工作，同时还在学中文。
examples.pinyin: Tā yìbiān gōngzuò, tóngshí hái zài xué Zhōngwén.
examples.english: She works and, at the same time, is also studying Chinese.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 提 is to lift or carry in the hand.
是 (shì) is a loose sound hint; the same part is in 题 tí and 堤 dī.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 供 is to supply or offer.
共 (gòng) sounds the same except tone; also in 恭 gōng and 洪 hóng.

example.hanzi: 学校为学生提供免费午餐。
example.pinyin: Xuéxiào wèi xuésheng tígōng miǎnfèi wǔcān.
example.english: The school provides free lunch for students.
example.fact: 提供 typically marks the recipient with 为 or 给 rather than stacking two objects directly after the verb — 为学生提供午餐 or 提供午餐给学生, but not a bare double-object 提供学生午餐 — a pattern worth drilling since English "provide someone something" allows exactly the structure Chinese avoids here.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā jiǔdiàn tígōng zǎocān.
examples.english: This hotel provides breakfast.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng tígōng yìxiē bāngzhù ma?
examples.english: Can you offer some help?

components.note: 女 (woman) — traditional reading shows an axe-like weapon 戌 over a woman 女, hence power and authority; compare 姑 and 妈.
⺼ (flesh, form of 月) — body parts: 脑, 脚, 肚; 胁 first meant the ribs or flank.
办 (bàn) is only a stand-in for old 劦 (xié), the real sound part; same series 协 xié.

example.hanzi: 气候变化威胁着许多动物的生存。
example.pinyin: Qìhòu biànhuà wēixiézhe xǔduō dòngwù de shēngcún.
example.english: Climate change is threatening the survival of many animals.
example.fact: 威胁's two halves independently point toward force applied to a body: 威 combines a weapon 戌 with 女 to suggest armed intimidation, while 胁 (built on the flesh radical ⺼) evokes controlling someone physically, close to its literal meaning "ribs/flank" — together painting coercive threat as bodily domination.

examples.hanzi: 他威胁我说要告诉老师。
examples.pinyin: Tā wēixié wǒ shuō yào gàosu lǎoshī.
examples.english: He threatened me, saying he'd tell the teacher.

examples.hanzi: 污染威胁着我们的健康。
examples.pinyin: Wūrǎn wēixié zhe wǒmen de jiànkāng.
examples.english: Pollution threatens our health.

components.note: 车 (vehicle) — carrying by cart; also in 轮 wheel, 辆 for cars.
俞 (yú) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 愉 yú and 愈 yù.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen duì shū le bǐsài.
example.english: Our team lost the match.
example.fact: 输 means "to lose" a contest or bet, the opposite of 赢. Its original meaning of carrying goods lives on in 运输 (transport) and 输入 / 输出 (input / output), and 输液 means to get an IV drip.

examples.pinyin: Bié huīxīn, shū le kěyǐ zài lái.
examples.english: Don't lose heart; if you lose you can try again.

examples.hanzi: 我下棋总是输给我爸爸。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiàqí zǒngshì shū gěi wǒ bàba.
examples.english: I always lose to my dad at chess.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speaking, shouting: 叫, 吗, 喊; 号 is to call out, then a call-sign or number.
丂 (kǎo) is only a loose clue; it also appears in 考 kǎo and 巧 qiǎo.
石 (stone) — stones and minerals: 破, 研, 砖; 码 first meant stone weights, then numbers.
马 (mǎ) sounds exactly like 码; also in 吗, 骂 mà, 妈 mā.

example.pinyin: Nǐ de diànhuà hàomǎ shì duōshao?
example.english: What's your phone number?
example.fact: 号码 names an identifying number treated as a label — a phone number, room number, ID number — while 数字 is reserved for digits or figures used in counting and math; reaching for 数字 to ask someone's phone number is a common learner mix-up.

examples.hanzi: 请把房间号码写在这儿。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ fángjiān hàomǎ xiě zài zhèr.
examples.english: Please write the room number here.

examples.hanzi: 我记不住这么长的号码。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jì bu zhù zhème cháng de hàomǎ.
examples.english: I can't remember such a long number.

components.note: 日 (sun, day) — a picture of the sun, once round with a dot, now squared off. As a radical it marks light and time: 明, 晴, 时.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.pinyin: Tāmen guòzhe xìngfú de rìzi.
example.english: They are living a happy life.
example.fact: 日子 stretches beyond a single calendar date to mean "the days of one's life," which is why 过日子 (guò rìzi, literally "to pass one's days") is the everyday idiom for "to get by" or "to live one's life" — a sense the more literal 天 ("day," as a count) doesn't carry.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān shì ge hǎo rìzi.
examples.english: Today is a good day.

examples.hanzi: 我们约个日子一起吃饭吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yuē ge rìzi yìqǐ chīfàn ba.
examples.english: Let's pick a date and have a meal together.

meanings: measure word for mountains and buildings

components.note: 广 (building) — 广 is a building or roof, as in 店, 床, 库; 座 is a seat in a hall.
坐 (zuò) — same sound — 座 is zuò, like 坐 (to sit).

example.pinyin: Qǐngwèn, zhège zuòwèi yǒu rén ma?
example.english: Excuse me, is this seat taken?
example.fact: 座 is a seat, but it is also the measure word for large, fixed things: 一座山, 一座桥, 一座城市. It appears in 座位 (seat), 讲座 (lecture) and in star-sign names like 天蝎座.

examples.pinyin: Qiánmiàn yǒu yí zuò hěn gāo de shān.
examples.english: There's a very tall mountain ahead.

examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de zuòwèi dōu zuò mǎn le.
examples.english: All the seats here are taken.

components.note: 比 (compare) — two people side by side, one lined up with the other; to compare.
女 (woman) — women and family terms, as in 妈 mom, 好 good, 姐 sister; 女 (nǚ) also loosely echoes the rú sound.
口 (mouth) — speech; 如 originally meant "to follow, accord with", later "as, like"; also in 汝 rǔ and 茹 rú.

example.hanzi: 很多水果都很甜,比如西瓜和芒果。
example.pinyin: Hěnduō shuǐguǒ dōu hěn tián, bǐrú xīguā hé mángguǒ.
example.english: Many fruits are sweet, for example watermelon and mango.
example.fact: 比如 sits at the conversational end of Chinese's "for example" words — its cousin 例如 carries the same meaning but leans more formal and written, useful to know when picking the right register for giving an example.

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢运动，比如游泳和跑步。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan yùndòng, bǐrú yóuyǒng hé pǎobù.
examples.english: I like sports, such as swimming and running.

examples.hanzi: 你能说说你的想法吗？比如工作方面。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng shuōshuo nǐ de xiǎngfǎ ma? Bǐrú gōngzuò fāngmiàn.
examples.english: Can you share your thoughts, for example about work?

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speaking and asking, as in 吗, 呢, 问: 哪 is a question word.
那 (nà) gives the same syllable in a different tone; compare 那 "that" and 哪 "which".
人 (person) — the top part. 个 is the general measure word, as in 一个, 这个, 那个.
丨 (a vertical tally) — under 人, read as one tally mark per person: counting individuals one by one.

example.hanzi: 这两件衬衫,你喜欢哪个?
example.pinyin: Zhè liǎng jiàn chènshān, nǐ xǐhuan nǎge?
example.english: Of these two shirts, which one do you like?
example.fact: 哪个 pairs the question word 哪 ("which") with 个, Mandarin's default measure word — the same "question word + 个" pattern behind 这个/那个 elsewhere in this deck — though a more specific classifier (哪件, 哪本) is used when the noun calls for one.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào nǎge?
examples.english: Which one do you want?

examples.pinyin: Nǎge shì nǐ de bāo?
examples.english: Which one is your bag?

components.note: 刂 (knife) — cutting and blades: 利, 别, 到; 剩 is what remains after cutting.
乘 (chéng) is close to shèng; also in 盛 shèng.
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.

example.hanzi: 蛋糕吃了一半,剩下的放冰箱里。
example.pinyin: Dàngāo chīle yíbàn, shèngxià de fàng bīngxiāng lǐ.
example.english: Half the cake got eaten; put what's left in the fridge.
example.fact: 剩下 is a verb plus result-complement: 剩 alone already means "to be left over," and 下 adds a sense of settling or remaining in place — the same verb + 下 pattern seen in 留下 ("to leave behind") and 坐下 ("to sit down").

examples.pinyin: Qián huāwán le, zhǐ shèngxià shí kuài.
examples.english: I've spent the money and only ten yuan is left.

examples.pinyin: Shèngxià de zuòyè míngtiān zài xiě.
examples.english: I'll do the rest of the homework tomorrow.

components.note: 厂 (cliff) — the visible frame, as in 原, 厚. Memory aid: a stern cliff face — 严重 serious, 严格 strict. Cliff family hint, not proven.
嚴 (traditional) — a larger shape with two mouths 吅 shouting orders. 严 cut it to 亚 plus 厂, losing the clue.
重 (zhòng) is a sound clue for 种 zhǒng/zhòng; it means heavy (zhòng) or to repeat (chóng, as in 重新).

example.pinyin: Zhè cì jiāotōng shìgù hěn yánzhòng.
example.english: This traffic accident was very serious.
example.fact: 严重 describes how grave a problem, illness, or situation is, but never a person's manner or personality — for a "serious" demeanor, Chinese instead reaches for 严肃, a split that English's single word "serious" glosses over.

examples.pinyin: Tā de bìng hěn yánzhòng.
examples.english: His illness is very serious.

examples.hanzi: 这个问题比你想的更严重。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge wèntí bǐ nǐ xiǎng de gèng yánzhòng.
examples.english: This problem is more serious than you think.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings and thoughts, as in 想, 思, 急; 感 is to feel or be moved.
咸 (xián) is a loose sound clue for gǎn; 咸 also sounds out 喊 hǎn and 减 jiǎn.

example.pinyin: Wǒ gǎndào hěn gāoxìng.
example.english: I feel very happy.
example.fact: 感 attaches to many nouns as a suffix meaning "sense of": 安全感 (sense of security), 幸福感 (happiness), 责任感 (responsibility). It also builds 感觉 (to feel), 感谢 (thank) and 感冒 (to catch a cold).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gǎnjué yǒudiǎn lèi.
examples.english: I feel a bit tired.

examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ, wǒ hěn gǎndòng.
examples.english: Thank you, I'm very moved.

components.note: 享 (enjoy) — a picture of an ancestral hall where offerings were shared, hence to enjoy; it also appears in 亨 hēng and 郭 guō.
又 (hand) — two hands pass a vessel: one gives, one receives; 授 shòu adds 扌 for "give".

example.hanzi: 周末我喜欢在家享受安静的时光。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ xǐhuan zài jiā xiǎngshòu ānjìng de shíguāng.
example.english: On weekends I like to enjoy quiet time at home.
example.fact: 享 alone means "to partake of, to be granted" and 受 alone means "to receive" — together 享受 frames enjoyment as something received and savored rather than something actively chased, a gentler image than the more effortful 追求 ("to pursue").

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào xuéhuì xiǎngshòu shēnghuó.
examples.english: We should learn to enjoy life.

examples.hanzi: 坐在海边，我享受着温暖的阳光。
examples.pinyin: Zuò zài hǎibiān, wǒ xiǎngshòuzhe wēnnuǎn de yángguāng.
examples.english: Sitting by the sea, I enjoyed the warm sunshine.

components.note: 戈 (halberd, weapon) — war and weapons: 我, 成, 武, 伐; here fighting.
占 (zhàn) sounds exactly like 战; also in 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.
争 (contend) — simplified from 爭, two hands pulling at the same object. See 战争 war and 竞争 compete.

example.hanzi: 这部电影讲述了一场战争的故事。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎngshùle yì chǎng zhànzhēng de gùshi.
example.english: This movie tells the story of a war.
example.fact: 战争 takes the measure word 场 (chǎng), the same classifier used for large-scale events like sports matches and rainstorms — a reminder that Chinese measure words often group nouns by scale or shape rather than by category.

examples.hanzi: 战争给人们带来了很多痛苦。
examples.pinyin: Zhànzhēng gěi rénmen dàiláile hěn duō tòngkǔ.
examples.english: War brought people a great deal of suffering.

examples.hanzi: 我们都希望世界没有战争。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen dōu xīwàng shìjiè méiyǒu zhànzhēng.
examples.english: We all hope the world has no war.

components.note: 心 (heart; bottom form ⺗) — feelings: 想, 思, 感; 恭 is a respectful heart.
共 (gòng) gives the sound, same except tone; also in 供 gōng and 洪 hóng.
壴 (zhù, drum) — a drum on top of 口 mouth: music and singing, joy.
口 (mouth) — singing and speaking, as in 唱 sing, 吃 eat.

example.pinyin: Gōngxǐ nǐ kǎoshàngle dàxué!
example.english: Congratulations on getting into university!
example.fact: 恭喜 anchors the standard Chinese New Year greeting 恭喜发财 ("congratulations, may you prosper") — one of the clearest everyday windows into 恭喜's specifically celebratory, good-news register, distinct from a plain politeness word.

examples.pinyin: Gōngxǐ nǐmen jiéhūn!
examples.english: Congratulations on your marriage!

examples.pinyin: Gōngxǐ fācái!
examples.english: Wishing you prosperity!

components.note: 乂 (to cut, crisscross) — old for mowing or cutting. Dictionary story: someone cut down 乂 and buried in a wooden coffin 木, a vivid memory aid.
木 (tree, wood) — the bottom. In 杀 it is a leftover of the old 殺 form rather than meaning wood; 殺 also had 殳 (weapon in hand).
歹 (bad bone) — death and decay, as in 残 remnant, 烈 fierce, 殊 special.
匕 (person) — a person beside bones: death.

example.hanzi: 医生想办法杀死癌细胞。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng xiǎng bànfǎ shāsǐ ái xìbāo.
example.english: Doctors look for ways to kill cancer cells.
example.fact: Adding 死 after 杀 makes the killing's outcome explicit — 杀 alone can describe an attack without confirming the target actually died — placing 杀死 in a family of verb + 死 resultative compounds that includes 淹死 ("to drown") and 冻死 ("to freeze to death").

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yào kěyǐ shāsǐ xìjūn.
examples.english: This medicine can kill bacteria.

examples.hanzi: 不要杀死那只虫子，把它放到外面去。
examples.pinyin: Búyào shāsǐ nà zhī chóngzi, bǎ tā fàng dào wàimiàn qù.
examples.english: Don't kill that bug, put it outside.

components.note: 其 (its) — an old picture of a winnowing basket (箕 jī adds bamboo). Sound clue: 期 qī, 旗 qí, 棋 qí, 欺 qī, 基 jī.

example.hanzi: 其中有一个是我的朋友。
example.pinyin: Qízhōng yǒu yí gè shì wǒ de péngyou.
example.english: One of them is my friend.
example.fact: 其 is a classical pronoun meaning "his / her / its / their" that survives mostly in fixed words: 其中 (among them), 其他 (other), 其实 (actually), 尤其 (especially), 其次 (secondly). It is rarely used as a free word in speech.

examples.pinyin: Qítā rén dōu yǐjīng zǒu le.
examples.english: Everyone else has already left.

examples.hanzi: 他把书给了我，并告诉了我其用法。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ shū gěi le wǒ, bìng gàosu le wǒ qí yòngfǎ.
examples.english: He gave me the book and told me how to use it.

components.note: 彡 (strokes of light or hair) — shining or decoration, as in 形 shape, 彩 colour, 须 beard.
景 (jǐng) is a close sound clue for yǐng; 景 itself meant light; 影 is its shadow.
口 (mouth) — sound and speech: 吗, 叫, 喊; 响 is a sound or echo.
向 (xiàng) matches the sound except tone; also in 饷 xiǎng.

example.hanzi: 睡眠不足会影响你的健康。
example.pinyin: Shuìmián bùzú huì yǐngxiǎng nǐ de jiànkāng.
example.english: Lack of sleep can affect your health.
example.fact: 影响 literally pairs "shadow" (影) with "echo" (响) — two things that trail an original cause without ever touching it directly, a fitting image behind a word that describes an effect propagating outward from its source.

examples.pinyin: Tiānqì huì yǐngxiǎng wǒ de xīnqíng.
examples.english: The weather affects my mood.

examples.hanzi: 父母对孩子的影响很大。
examples.pinyin: Fùmǔ duì háizi de yǐngxiǎng hěn dà.
examples.english: Parents have a great influence on their children.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — crops and harvests: 秋 autumn, 种 plant, 秒 second; 利 shows grain 禾 cut with a blade 刂, hence profit and sharp.
用 (use) — early picture is debated: a pail, a fenced enclosure or a hung bell. Memory aid: a door-frame 冂 with a cross-bar — a tool 'put to use' (使用, 不用).

example.hanzi: 他利用假期学习了法语。
example.pinyin: Tā lìyòng jiàqī xuéxíle Fǎyǔ.
example.english: He made use of his vacation to study French.
example.fact: 利用 can describe resourcefully making the most of something (利用假期, "made use of the vacation") or exploiting someone in a self-serving way (利用别人, "to use/exploit someone") — one word covers both the neutral-positive and the negative sense, and only context decides which.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào hǎohāo lìyòng shíjiān.
examples.english: We should make good use of our time.

examples.pinyin: Tā lìyòng wǎngluò zuò shēngyi.
examples.english: He uses the internet to do business.

components.note: 忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid; 恨 is hatred in the heart.
艮 (gèn) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 很 hěn, 根 gēn and 跟 gēn.

example.hanzi: 我恨自己没有早点告诉你。
example.pinyin: Wǒ hèn zìjǐ méiyǒu zǎodiǎn gàosu nǐ.
example.english: I hate myself for not telling you sooner.
example.fact: 恨 is stronger than 讨厌 (to dislike) and carries real resentment or regret. The pattern 恨不得 ("hate that one cannot") expresses an intense wish: 我恨不得马上回家, "I can't wait to go home right now".

examples.hanzi: 我不恨他，只是有点失望。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú hèn tā, zhǐshì yǒudiǎn shīwàng.
examples.english: I don't hate him; I'm just a bit disappointed.

examples.pinyin: Tā hènbude mǎshàng huí jiā.
examples.english: He can't wait to go home right now.

components.note: 乂 (to cut, crisscross) — old for mowing or cutting. Dictionary story: someone cut down 乂 and buried in a wooden coffin 木, a vivid memory aid.
木 (tree, wood) — the bottom. In 杀 it is a leftover of the old 殺 form rather than meaning wood; 殺 also had 殳 (weapon in hand).
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 警方正在调查一起杀人案。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài diàochá yì qǐ shārén àn.
example.english: Police are investigating a murder case.
example.fact: 杀人 is a verb-object compound (杀 "to kill" + 人 "person") loose enough to still take material worked in, as in 杀人犯 ("murderer," literally "kill-person offender") — a flexibility that a fully fused synonym like 谋杀 ("to murder") doesn't share.

examples.pinyin: Shārén shì fànfǎ de.
examples.english: Killing a person is against the law.

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢看关于杀人案的小说。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan kàn guānyú shārén'àn de xiǎoshuō.
examples.english: I like reading novels about murder cases.

components.note: 月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the body radical (月 in 脸, 脑); 脱 is slipping off a layer, like skin or clothes.
兑 (duì) — near sound — 脱 is tuō; 兑 also sounds out 说 shuō and 税 shuì.

example.pinyin: Jìn mén qǐng tuō xié.
example.english: Please take off your shoes when you come in.
example.fact: 脱 is the verb for removing clothes, shoes and hats (opposite of 穿 or 戴). Figuratively it means getting free of something: 脱离 (break away from), 脱口而出 (blurt out), and the slang 脱单 ("leave singlehood").

examples.hanzi: 天太热了，我想把外套脱了。
examples.pinyin: Tiān tài rè le, wǒ xiǎng bǎ wàitào tuō le.
examples.english: It's so hot that I want to take off my coat.

examples.hanzi: 他脱下帽子，向大家问好。
examples.pinyin: Tā tuō xià màozi, xiàng dàjiā wènhǎo.
examples.english: He took off his hat and greeted everyone.

components.note: 阝 (mound, left-side form of 阜 hill) — hills and places: 院, 阳, 陆; 陪 is to sit by one's side.
咅 (pōu) is a loose sound clue; same part in 培 péi, 赔 péi, 倍 bèi.

example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ péi māma qù kànbìng.
example.english: On the weekend I go with my mother to see the doctor.
example.fact: 陪 always needs a person to accompany: 陪我, 陪孩子玩, 陪客人. It implies keeping someone company for their sake, unlike 跟, which just means "with". 陪伴 is a warmer, more literary "companionship".

examples.hanzi: 你不用陪我，我自己去就行。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ búyòng péi wǒ, wǒ zìjǐ qù jiù xíng.
examples.english: You don't need to come with me; I can go myself.

examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ péi wǒ liáotiān.
examples.english: Thanks for keeping me company while chatting.

components.note: 夫 (man) — the main part. Dictionary reading: something 丿 slipping from a hand. Memory aid: a man 夫 dropping what he held — 失去 to lose.
⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and walking: 跑, 跳, 路; 踪 is a footprint or trace.
宗 (zōng) sounds exactly like 踪; also in 综 zōng and 棕 zōng.

example.pinyin: Nà sōu chuán zài hǎishàng shīzōng le.
example.english: That ship went missing at sea.
example.fact: 踪 on its own means "tracks, traces" (as in 踪迹, "footprints, trace") — so 失踪 literally means "to lose one's tracks," painting someone vanishing so completely that not even a trail remains, the vivid image behind the everyday word for "missing."

examples.pinyin: Tā de péngyou tūrán shīzōng le.
examples.english: His friend suddenly went missing.

examples.hanzi: 警察正在寻找失踪的孩子。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhèngzài xúnzhǎo shīzōng de háizi.
examples.english: The police are looking for the missing child.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; recognising something is naming it.
人 (rén) gives the exact sound, and also means "person".
真 (zhēn) is a sound clue for 镇 zhèn and 慎 shèn; 真 means real, true.

example.pinyin: Tā gōngzuò yìzhí hěn rènzhēn.
example.english: He has always been very conscientious in his work.
example.fact: 认真 usually describes an attitude toward doing a specific task carefully (认真学习, "study earnestly") rather than a fixed personality trait, sitting closer to English "diligent" or "earnest" than to 严重's problem-focused "serious" (also in this batch), even though dictionaries sometimes gloss both as "serious."

examples.pinyin: Xuéxí yào rènzhēn.
examples.english: You have to be serious about studying.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ rènzhēn de tīng wǒ shuō hǎo ma?
examples.english: Could you listen to me seriously?

components.note: 真 (zhēn) is a sound clue for 镇 zhèn and 慎 shèn; 真 means real, true.
目 (eye) — looking; an eye turned on a tree 木, hence to look at, and mutually looking: "each other". 相 also gives 想 xiǎng, 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.

example.hanzi: 记者们想找出事件的真相。
example.pinyin: Jìzhěmen xiǎng zhǎochū shìjiàn de zhēnxiàng.
example.english: The reporters wanted to find out the truth behind the incident.
example.fact: 真相 specifically names a hidden or underlying truth waiting to be uncovered — the reason it shows up constantly in detective stories and scandal reporting — rather than a plain factual statement, which is why the set phrase 真相大白 ("the truth comes to light") reads almost cinematically.

examples.pinyin: Zhēnxiàng zhōngyú dàbái le.
examples.english: The truth finally came out.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhīdào shìqing de zhēnxiàng ma?
examples.english: Do you know the truth about the matter?

components.note: 氵 (water) — water, as in 河, 海, 清: in the old form 灋, water stood for fairness, so law and method.
彳 (step) — walking and conduct, as in 行, 往, 得, 很.
聿 (brush) — writing the rules: 律 is law, and a rule of rhythm.

example.hanzi: 每个人都应该遵守法律。
example.pinyin: Měi gè rén dōu yīnggāi zūnshǒu fǎlǜ.
example.english: Everyone should obey the law.
example.fact: 律 is properly pronounced with the ü umlaut, lǜ — after l and n the dots can never be dropped the way they are after j/q/x/y, since lu/lü and nu/nü are genuinely different syllables (律 lǜ versus, say, 卢 lú) that would otherwise collide.

examples.pinyin: Fǎlǜ miànqián rénrén píngděng.
examples.english: Everyone is equal before the law.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài dàxué xuéxí fǎlǜ.
examples.english: He studies law at university.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and teaching: 说, 请, 课; 训 is instruction.
川 (chuān) is only a loose sound hint; 训 shares its part with 顺 shùn.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 给, 线; 练 first meant boiling silk to soften it, then practice.
柬 (jiǎn) is a loose sound clue; same part in 炼 liàn and 简 jiǎn.

example.pinyin: Yùndòngyuán měitiān dōu yào xùnliàn.
example.english: Athletes have to train every day.
example.fact: 训 alone means "to instruct" (as in 教训, "lesson, to reprimand") while 练 alone means "to practice, to drill" (as in 练习) — 训练 pairs an instructional half with a practice half, describing guided, structured practice rather than solo repetition.

examples.pinyin: Jiàoliàn zhèngzài xùnliàn xīn duìyuán.
examples.english: The coach is training the new team members.

examples.hanzi: 每周三有两个小时的训练。
examples.pinyin: Měi zhōu sān yǒu liǎng ge xiǎoshí de xùnliàn.
examples.english: There are two hours of training every Wednesday.

components.note: 米 (rice) — a picture of grains of rice divided by a line; as a radical it marks grain foods, as in 粉 powder, 粮 grain, 糖 sugar.

example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān dōu chī mǐfàn.
example.english: I eat rice every day.
example.fact: 米 is uncooked rice or grain, while cooked rice is 饭 (米饭). It is also the everyday word for the metre: 一米八 (1.8 metres) is how people give their height, and 百米 is the 100-metre race.

examples.hanzi: 米饭还没做好，请再等一会儿。
examples.pinyin: Mǐfàn hái méi zuò hǎo, qǐng zài děng yíhuìr.
examples.english: The rice isn't ready yet; please wait a bit longer.

examples.pinyin: Zhège fángjiān yǒu sì mǐ cháng.
examples.english: This room is four metres long.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 值 is worth.
直 (zhí) sounds exactly like 值; also 植 zhí and 置 zhì.
彳 (step) — walking and going, as in 行, 往, 很 very.
寸 (hand) — oldest form is a hand grabbing a cowrie shell (money): 得 is "to obtain". The shell has worn down to 旦.

example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng hěn zhíde yí kàn.
example.english: This movie is well worth watching.
example.fact: 值得 slots directly in front of a verb phrase to mean "worth doing X" (值得一看, "worth watching"; 值得尝试, "worth trying") — a compact construction that English can only match by adding a separate gerund after "worth."

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de cài zhídé yí shì.
examples.english: The food at this restaurant is worth trying.

examples.pinyin: Zhè diǎn xiǎoshì bù zhídé shēngqì.
examples.english: This little thing isn't worth getting angry about.

components.note: 主 (master, host) — a lamp with a flame on top; a lamp stand was the centre of the room. 主 also sounds out 注 zhù, 住 zhù and 柱 zhù.

example.pinyin: Tā shì zhè jiā diàn de zhǔrén.
example.english: He is the owner of this shop.
example.fact: 主 means the one in charge or the main thing: 主人 (host, owner), 主要 (main), 主意 (idea, decision), 主任 (director). 主意 is a good one to know: 拿主意 means "make up one's mind".

examples.pinyin: Tā shì gōngsī de zhǔguǎn.
examples.english: He is the manager of the company.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì zhǔyào shì wǒ de cuò.
examples.english: This matter is mainly my fault.

components.note: 月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.
心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.
田 here replaces 囟 (skull) in the older form: head over heart
心 (heart) — thinking and feeling, as in 想, 意, 感: 思 is to think over, with head and heart.

example.hanzi: 这本书的故事很有意思。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn shū de gùshi hěn yǒuyìsi.
example.english: The story in this book is very interesting.
example.fact: 有意思 literally combines "to have" (有) with "meaning/interest" (意思) — its negation, casually shortened to 没意思, means "boring, meaningless," the flip side of the same "has/lacks meaning" image.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de bǐsài hěn yǒu yìsi.
examples.english: Today's match was very interesting.

examples.hanzi: 他是一个很有意思的人。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí ge hěn yǒu yìsi de rén.
examples.english: He is a very interesting person.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — 灬 is fire at the bottom, as in 点, 照, 熟; 热 is heat.

example.pinyin: Jīntiān tiānqì hěn rè.
example.english: The weather is very hot today.
example.fact: 热 describes heat of weather, food and drinks, whereas very hot to the touch is 烫. It also means "popular": 热门 (hot topic), 热销 (selling well), and 热闹 means lively and bustling. Drinking 热水 (hot water) is a daily habit in China.

examples.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, shuǐ hěn rè, bié tàngzhe.
examples.english: Careful, the water is hot; don't burn yourself.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ niúnǎi rè yíxià.
examples.english: Please heat up the milk.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and roles: 你, 他, 位; 使 is sending someone to do something.
吏 (lì, official) gives the meaning, and shares its ancestor 史 (shǐ), the exact sound of 使.
用 (use) — early picture is debated: a pail, a fenced enclosure or a hung bell. Memory aid: a door-frame 冂 with a cross-bar — a tool 'put to use' (使用, 不用).

example.hanzi: 请按照说明使用这台机器。
example.pinyin: Qǐng ànzhào shuōmíng shǐyòng zhè tái jīqì.
example.english: Please use this machine according to the instructions.
example.fact: 使用 is the more formal, often written register for "to use" a tool or method, while everyday spoken Mandarin defaults to the plainer 用 for the same idea — a register gap similar to English "utilize" versus "use."

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge ruǎnjiàn hěn róngyì shǐyòng.
examples.english: This software is very easy to use.

examples.pinyin: Kǎoshì shí bù néng shǐyòng shǒujī.
examples.english: You can't use your phone during the exam.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — the sheep family: 美, 养, 群. Dictionary story: work 工 done by a sheep — memory aid for being poor or off. Origin uncertain.
工 (work) — the bottom. Memory aid: poor work 工, so 差劲 poor quality. 差 is chā/chà (difference, lacking) or chāi (send).

example.pinyin: Xiànzài chà wǔ fēn bā diǎn.
example.english: It's five to eight now.
example.fact: 差 has three readings: chà (poor, lacking), chā (difference, as in 差别) and chāi (errand, as in 出差). Chà is how you tell time: 差五分八点 means "five minutes short of eight". 差不多 (almost the same) is read chà too.

examples.hanzi: 这次考试，我差两分就及格了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì kǎoshì, wǒ chà liǎng fēn jiù jígé le.
examples.english: I was two points short of passing this exam.

examples.pinyin: Tā de Hànyǔ bǐ wǒ chà duō le.
examples.english: His Chinese is much worse than mine.

components.note: 方 (square, direction) — early picture is disputed (a plough-like tool or lashed boats). Sound clue in 房 fáng, 防 fáng, 访 fǎng, 放 fàng.
亠 (lid) — the top. Memory aid: a lid over a bent shape — a square-cornered 'side' or place, as in 地方, 方法.
面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.

example.hanzi: 在健康方面,他非常小心。
example.pinyin: Zài jiànkāng fāngmiàn, tā fēicháng xiǎoxīn.
example.english: When it comes to health, he is very careful.
example.fact: 方面 typically follows a noun to frame "in the respect/area of X" (健康方面, "health-wise") — a common sentence-opening move that lets a speaker narrow down which angle of a topic they mean before saying anything else about it.

examples.hanzi: 在学习方面，她从不让父母担心。
examples.pinyin: Zài xuéxí fāngmiàn, tā cóng bú ràng fùmǔ dānxīn.
examples.english: When it comes to studying, she never makes her parents worry.

examples.hanzi: 我们要从多个方面考虑这个问题。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào cóng duō ge fāngmiàn kǎolǜ zhè ge wèntí.
examples.english: We need to consider this problem from several aspects.

components.note: 钅 (metal, simplified 金) — metals and money: 钱, 铁, 钢; 银 is silver.
艮 (gèn) is only a loose sound hint; the same part is in 根 gēn and 眼 yǎn.
彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.

example.pinyin: Wǒ xūyào qù yínháng qǔ qián.
example.english: I need to go to the bank to withdraw money.
example.fact: 行 is a classic multi-reading character: pronounced xíng it means "to go, OK, will do" (as in the stand-alone reply 行!, "sure, that works"), but pronounced háng it names an orderly row or a professional trade — the háng reading is the one locked into 银行 ("bank") and 行业 ("industry").

examples.hanzi: 这家银行星期天也开门。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā yínháng xīngqītiān yě kāimén.
examples.english: This bank is open on Sundays too.

examples.hanzi: 我想在银行开一个账户。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng zài yínháng kāi yí ge zhànghù.
examples.english: I'd like to open an account at the bank.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 怕; 恐 is fear.
巩 (gǒng) is a near sound match (-ong).
忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 怕 afraid, 情 emotion, 快 happy; 怖 is terror.
布 (bù) sounds exactly like 怖; also in 部 bù.

example.hanzi: 那部恐怖电影把我吓坏了。
example.pinyin: Nà bù kǒngbù diànyǐng bǎ wǒ xiàhuài le.
example.english: That horror movie scared me badly.
example.fact: 恐怖 reduplicates the idea of fear across both halves — 恐 alone means "to dread" and 怖 alone also means "terrified" — the same intensifying, two-near-synonym structure behind 喜欢 ("to like") elsewhere in this deck; 恐怖片 specifically names the horror-film genre.

examples.pinyin: Shēnyè de yīyuàn yǒudiǎn kǒngbù.
examples.english: The hospital at midnight is a bit creepy.

examples.hanzi: 他给我讲了一个恐怖的故事。
examples.pinyin: Tā gěi wǒ jiǎngle yí ge kǒngbù de gùshi.
examples.english: He told me a frightening story.

components.note: 尺 (chǐ, ruler) — the visible top part, as in 尺寸 size. 尽 simplifies 盡 and the shape does not explain 'use up'. Memory aid: measure it to the very end.

example.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng jìnlì le.
example.english: I have already done my best.
example.fact: 尽 has two readings: jìn means to exhaust or do to the fullest (尽力, 用尽), while jǐn means "as much as possible" (尽快, 尽量). Learners often read 尽快 with jìn by mistake; it is jǐnkuài, "as soon as possible".

examples.pinyin: Tā jǐnkuài bǎ gōngzuò zuò wán le.
examples.english: He finished the work as fast as he could.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng jǐnliàng shuō màn yìdiǎn.
examples.english: Please try to speak a bit slower.

meanings: so, actually, as it turns out

components.note: 厂 (cliff) — cliffs and rocks, as in 厅 hall, 厚 thick: a spring flowing from a cliff.
泉 (spring) — water from the rock: the source (源 yuán adds 氵 later); 原 is source, origin.
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.

example.hanzi: 我原来打算八点出发,但是迟到了。
example.pinyin: Wǒ yuánlái dǎsuan bā diǎn chūfā, dànshì chídào le.
example.english: I had originally planned to leave at eight, but I ended up being late.
example.fact: Beyond its literal "originally," 原来 doubles as a mid-sentence realization marker meaning "oh, so that's how it is" (原来是这样啊!) — a jump from describing the past to voicing sudden understanding that learners who only memorize the first sense often miss.

examples.pinyin: Yuánlái shì nǐ a!
examples.english: So it was you!

examples.hanzi: 我原来住在上海，现在住在北京。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yuánlái zhù zài Shànghǎi, xiànzài zhù zài Běijīng.
examples.english: I used to live in Shanghai, but now I live in Beijing.
